segments: So I am here with Calvin Parker, and we're going to be talking about his incredible experience,
the Pascagoula incident, and yes, the first question, it all started with your friend Charles Hickson getting you a job.
Yeah, actually, Charlie wasn't a friend. He was like a, he was a lot older than I was.
He was 42 years old. I was 18 years old, and I was working in the oil field, and this thing sounds terrible.
Turn it down just a little.
All right, I was working in the oil field seven days a week, 16 hours a day.
I was going to get married the next month, so I called Charlie up.
Daddy said to call Charlie and ask him for a job, and he'd give me a real reasonable job, which I like working.
So anyhow, he said, come on down, and we will, I got an opening for a ship fitter and a welder.
So you come to the Mississippi Gulf Coast to Pascagoula.
We'll go to work at the shipyard.
I went down that night, and to make a long story short, my job lasted one day.
I got hired, fired, and took a physical all in the same day.
And I'll get into that in a little bit.
Right, and well, what had happened, which I know one of your favorite pastimes is fishing.
I've talked to you, and you've shared that with me quite a bit.
So after work, your first day at the job, you decided to go.
You and Charlie decided to go fishing, and that's when all the weirdness happened.
We had worked all day long, got off, and it was hot.
Well, nobody feels like going straight home when you get off work, you know.
So he wanted to go cool down.
He said, Calvin, let's go fishing.
I said, sure, that sounds good to me.
Charlie, I didn't bring no fishing equipment with me.
Let's go by the house and pick mine up.
Now, in the south, that's a mortal sin to use somebody else's fishing equipment.
But I agreed to for that one day.
So we went by and picked up the fishing equipment, and that's where we started.
We got in the car, and we rode down to what they call the Shaw Peter Shipyard in Paspergoula.
And it was an old abandoned shipyard.
And when you pull up and just look at it, you'd say, gosh, these people don't care what their shipyard looks like or nothing, because it was a mess.
But Charlie later explained to me on the way, while we was trying to work our way down to the fishing pier, what happened.
We get floodwaters on the Paspergoula River, and the water will come up, and it brings all this trash in.
And then when it goes out, it leaves it where it was.
And this was a mess right there.
And this part's important, you know, during the story.
It tells about the no trespassing signs and all that we had seen, and explains a little of why, you know, I was kind of afraid when this first happened.
But when this happened, we made it down to the river, and as we was fishing, we got casted out river.
But we noticed some blue, hazy lights coming from behind us.
And I thought, now, I read the no trespassing sign.
Did this idiot bring me down here knowing we was going to jail tonight?
And I thought, yeah, that's where I'm headed.
So I said, Charlie, the law's back there.
Are they fixing to get us?
So we both stood up about the same time and turned around.
Gosh, I wish it had been the law.
Then that's when a bright light all of a sudden just appeared out of nowhere.
It was so bright it was blinding.
And apparently this is where them three robotic-looking creatures came out of to pick us up.
Now, I didn't notice them to start with because the light was bright, and it was just slamming my eyes, and my eyes was hurting.
But three of them floated across the top of the grass, and they came over, and two of them got a hold of Charlie, and one got a hold of myself.
While I was trying to get behind Charlie after seeing that, there wasn't nowhere to run.
We had water and junk in the front of us.
We had water on the side, both sides, and we had a mess of junk in behind us.
So we had no choice but to go on board.
So these things got a hold of us, and I've always said they was robotic-looking.
Charlie actually said the same thing.
Because of the way they moved, they moved mechanical.
And this is why I started calling them the big, ugly ones, because they were big and ugly.
But they had, like, mittens or crab-like hands.
If anybody knows what a crab's claws looked like, that's kind of what they favored.
And they grabbed me by the left arm, and as soon as they did, I felt like an injection going into my arm.
Well, that just kind of numbed me.
I think they'd give me some pretty good dope or something.
But it kind of numbed me up, and they levitated us.
Now, this is when I lost sight of Charlie.
I didn't see Charlie until after we got back out.
But they levitated me toward the door, and in my mind, I was wondering, now, where's all this light coming from?
That was really amazing to me, but it was coming from the inside of the crowd.
And I was kind of able to squinch my eyes and look around a little bit in there, and I noticed there weren't no light fixtures.
It was coming, like, out of the walls, out of the paint.
So this thing kind of paused, and I thought about that a second.
And he made a little left turn.
Then he made a right turn.
And he took me into this examination room, what I'm going to call it.
I don't know what it was.
And he laid me on a, turned me around, laid me back about a 45-degree angle.
I didn't have nothing to measure.
But he laid me on this table, and I still couldn't move.
I was more or less paralyzed.
That's when it got real strange.
He backed up out of the way, and I kind of didn't really hear nothing, but out of the corner of my eye, I seen something coming toward me.
Now, this is what I call the female.
And I don't know if it's female or not.
You know, it's hard to tell.
The only thing I knew, I'd been to Bourbon Street enough and knew the difference between a male and a female, you know.
And as she approached me, I did.
I tried to look at her clothing and her build, and she just reminded me of a female.
Now, her fingers, her hands was like ours, where the other one had crab-like hands.
And her fingers, two middle fingers, were just a little longer.
I didn't see her legs move, because all I could do was roll my eyes in my head and notice her.
And you've seen these commercials where these grandkids, grandmother pieced her cheek like that.
I didn't feel any sensation at all.
No warmth, no coldness, nothing coming out of her hands.
And I still kind of thought that was strange, but I'm going to lay this on being doped up from the shot they gave me,
which later on in the examination office, you know, the medical examiner proved that.
And she grabbed me by the chin with one hand, and she pushed it down.
And that's when I changed my attitude about her.
I wasn't too afraid until then.
But she run these two long fingers down my throat.
And that little thing that hangs down in the back, she tried to come up behind it into my nasal cavity.
And later on, I found out she might have implanted something in there, because later on, you know, they tried to get it out.
But that's when I started choking, and my nose started bleeding.
And, I mean, I was getting scared then.
And if I was able, if I could have moved, I would have put the fear in her right then, but I couldn't move.
But then in another sense, she said in a calm voice, telepathically, and it was just like she was laying there talking to me in a real nice, calm voice.
We're not going to harm you.
And I thought, well, it's too late for that.
She done bleed blood in my nose.
She went behind my little hangy down in my throat and about ripped it out.
I said, this is terrible, lady.
And, you know, I was thinking back, and it was just like she was reading my mind.
And I feel like she was, because we was communicating mentally.
And her voice mentally spoke really good redneck English.
And, you know, so I know she had been around and tried to study us like that.
Because, you know, in different parts of the country, you hear different languages.
Like, I deal with a publisher from the U.K., and I can't understand the word that man says.
I go to Louisiana, I can't understand them.
I come up here to where the Yankees are, and I dang sure can't understand them.
They don't even know what grits are.
Her voice and what I'm trying to get at, the communication in her voice, it was soothing.
It was like a down south voice, and it kind of calmed me down then, you know, to listen to it.
I just felt like I was on a bad day then.
So, when she pulled her fingers out, my nose was bleeding.
My little thing that hangs down, it was just about pulled out.
As a matter of fact, it swelled up the next day, they had to take me to the emergency room.
And she pulled her hands out, and then she kind of backed up a little bit,
and she made a little mumbling noise, like a oomph, like that.
But when it did, that old big ugly one that was standing in the corner, apparently he did.
He came over and grabbed me by the left arm again,
and I felt the injection, like a shot or something.
And I got calmed down again.
And that's when they picked me up.
They levitated me back out to the pier that we was fishing on.
Now, a lot of people think we were in a boat, but we was actually on a fishing pier.
And that's when I, the first time I seen and heard Charlie when they got back out there.
And it's a long story on him from there.
But Charlie was on the ground.
He said, son, son, you okay?
And I wanted to say, no, you idiot, I'm not okay, you know.
It's just like somebody kicking the door down in your house and coming in and getting you
and taking you out to their van and running their fingers down your throat.
It was not a good experience for me.
But I really don't think they meant a lot of harm.
Now, commonly the creatures that you encountered are depicted as kind of having no face
and these cones kind of coming out of each side of their head.
Is that what you remember or is that Charlie's memory?
After we got back the next day to the shipyard from work,
there was an artist by the name of Larry Flynn sat down.
And he said, what did y'all see?
I said, I didn't see nothing.
Because I had told, we had talked about this.
Charlie and I had talked about this.
And we both agreed not to say nothing to nobody.
But Charlie went and he told Keesler and the sheriff's department.
But he described this creature to him.
And this artist drew it up.
Now, we've seen two different things.
Charlie got the basic build right.
But I didn't see all these things sticking out on the face.
And I figured they might have been antennas.
But it's a good possibility it was.
So, when you were back on the shore, is that when you decided to go to the sheriff or go to the police station to let them know what had happened to you?
Well, to be honest with you, when we got back and was at the pier, Charlie and I sat down and talked just a few minutes.
And Charlie says, well, we need to tell somebody.
I said, tell somebody what, Charlie?
We don't need to tell nobody nothing.
I said, I'm getting married in a month.
And I don't want to bring this publicity on me.
I don't want to lose my job.
I don't want to do this.
He said, well, we got to tell somebody.
So, we got in the car.
And as I was driving us back to the apartment, he said, pull over right here.
And I need to use it in just a minute.
I thought he was calling his wife.
I didn't know who he was calling.
Well, he come out and he said, they said to call the local authorities.
Back in, you didn't have cell phones.
So, I said, why do you need another dime?
Well, I called Keister Air Force Base.
They said, call the local authorities.
Now, I got to call the Jackson County Sheriff's Department.
So, that's how they came into play on this deal.
So, when you were brought, when you told your story at the police station, how was it taken?
How did you feel they were?
Well, when we first started, and we was still in the car in front of the store, they said, don't leave.
So, I know they thought we was drinking or on dope or something.
So, I took them at the word not to leave, and he said, we're going to send a car.
They got me out of the car and left Charlie sitting in the car.
Well, they made me do a sobriety test to see if I was drinking.
They said, look, stand up on one leg, bend your head back, touch your nose with your right hand, close your eyes, and count from 100 backwards.
I said, man, I can't do that sober.
They said, we just need to see if you can.
Then, he held a flashlight, and he said, follow it with your eyes.
He said, look, you seem all right.
Follow us to the sheriff's department.
So, we followed him to the sheriff's department.
That's how convinced he was that I was sober.
Then, they made me blow on a balloon or something in there.
And, I ain't never been so, had, I had good lungs back then, but it's hard to blow on one of them balloons you can't blow up.
So, anyhow, that's how we ended up there.
And so, when they left you all alone, I guess there was a, they tested you.
And, and how did that come about, and what resulted?
Well, they interrogated us separate to start with.
They took Charlie into a room, me into a room.
Then, they come out and got both of us, and they put us in the same room.
Well, while we was in this room, they had no idea, or we had no idea there was a tape recorder there.
And, by this time, I was getting scared, because I didn't like the law playing with me anyway.
And, I didn't like what had happened to me, and they didn't seem to be taken as serious.
So, Charlie and I were sitting in there talking.
Matter of fact, I was a real religious person then.
And, I said a little prayer, you know, God, please help me.
You know, I don't know what went on, but give me the strength and the power to overcome all this.
And, I felt like my prayers would be answered.
Then, on the other end, I said, feels like I stepped on a damn rattlesnake, Charlie.
And, that's how scared I was.
Then, the sheriff came in, and I seen him reach in a drawer, and he got this tape recorder out.
And, they must have went back and listened to it.
At this time, I still didn't know we was taped.
Charlie didn't realize we had been taped.
So, when they heard this tape, he come in, he said,
Son, I know y'all been through a lot.
I need to talk to you a little further.
I want you to settle down, and I need to see y'all tomorrow.
And, I said, okay, that's fine with me.
I said, but look, let's make a deal.
I know Charlie has told y'all what went on.
When y'all was interrogating me, I said I didn't remember nothing.
He said, well, look, I got evidence right here that you do remember something.
So, that's why I kept it quiet all these years.
I didn't want everybody to know.
Back in the 70s, there's two things you didn't talk about, politics and aliens.
So, that would get you in a lot of trouble.
So, that's why I kept quiet all these years.
And, Charlie took the upper road, you know, to go and do public speaking.
And, now that he did, I'm glad he did, but it caused a lot of hard feelings between Charlie and I.
I mean, I didn't talk to him for years.
So, at that time, I mean, had you ever heard of the concept of alien abduction?
The only thing I remember watching, we got three channels on TV, ABC, NBC, and CBS, was when the Apollo mission was going on.
And, I remembered, and that night when they picked me and Charlie up, you know, I remembered where they quarantined these beings.
I knew this wasn't from this world, or didn't think it was.
And, I remembered them quarantined them from their families for seven days.
And, that's why I begged Keesler, when they got a hold of us, and the sheriff's department, and anybody I could find, please lock me up.
I don't want to kill my family and my friends or nobody else's family.
Because, I just knew we had radiation or some kind of virus.
And, they took me at my word.
They, uh, they isolated us, took us to the hospital, Jackson County Hospital, did blood work, looked over the scars on my arm where it was ripped in two places where I got an injection.
And, uh, said they couldn't find anything bacterial wrong with us.
And, then, that's when the sheriff's department put us in the car and escorted us to Keesler Air Force Base for the radiation check.
We pulled up two Keesler, and these six guys outside, they had hazmat suits on.
And, you know, from a distance, these hazmat suits kind of looked about what I seen.
I told him, I said, give me your gun, and I ain't going up there to these people.
And, this deputy said, what do you mean?
Are they just going to check you for radiation?
I said, no, they ain't checking me.
He said, yeah, you need to go in here.
You might be contaminated, and we want to get you checked.
And, then, he explained who it was and where we were.
I didn't have a big education.
I didn't know much about what went on.
And, uh, to see stuff like this and to go through it, it just scared the living daylights out of you.
But, they checked us for radiation, and I heard them say, all clear.
And, then, they, when they said that, that's when they pulled their hazmat suits off.
And, they said, they need to see you in the back.
And, I just thought it would be two or three people to tell us about the radiation.
But, the room was a conference room like this, and it was full of Keesler Air Force Base officials, the local law enforcement, the mayors of every city on the Mississippi Gulf Coast.
It was full of people, and they wanted to ask questions.
I didn't want to answer questions, because by then, I was ready to have about a nervous breakdown.

I done handled all this stuff I could handle, because I knew I had done messed up at my job, because the guy that owned the company, when we got back there that same day after this, he said, look, maybe y'all need to take a couple of weeks off.
